summary: I found no Modine-specific filing, company release or contract news dated Oct 29-30, so today's 6.5 percent drop to 129.78 USD looks like the AI-infrastructure sell-off rather than a Modine fact; the B. Riley target cut to 285 from 305 (reported in your context, not found online by me) is a small change that sits inside the research. The stock is now about 4 percent above the 125 USD thesis-break price and about 23 percent below the research target (12m) of 169.01 USD, and Q2 results on Nov 3 after the close are unchanged.

items.headline: Price check: MOD closed 129.78 USD on Oct 30 (-6.49 percent from 138.79 USD; range 126.16-134.63 USD; volume 2.44M vs 1.43M average); 52-week range 111.18-323.25 USD
items.why: A price move with no new company fact behind it. The close is about 3.8 percent above the 125 USD thesis-break price, which the memo ties to a lost or deferred data-center customer agreement or an AI-spending down-cycle; today's move alone does not show either, and the falling price is not itself a trigger.

items.headline: B. Riley lowers Modine price target to 285 USD from 305 USD (as stated in the request context)
items.why: I could not find the Oct 29 note itself online; the URL is only an older B. Riley target page, not the cut. An analyst target change is a minor item already inside the research scenarios (bull case 243.88 USD, base 169.01 USD) and carries no new company facts.

items.headline: Search coverage: no article dated Oct 29-30 found on Modine, on an Intel-led AI-infrastructure sell-off (Intel -29 percent per request context), or on data-center cooling demand

The sector move therefore stays unverified from my side; it matches the AI-spending low case already weighted in the bear scenario (87.02 USD). Nothing here shows a customer cut or a delay to the data-center capacity agreement. Not sized.
